text: This page lists all the collectopaedia entries for The Ragmos Desolation. When filling in an entry, 8-9 Affinity Points will be rewarded.
Thirsty Oaks are Wood Collectibles in . They can be found in Vermilion Woods.
The Ancient Vessel is a Field Track from , composed by Manami Kiyota. It is track seven of disc one from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack. This song plays on the Ancient Ship.

The Beginning of Our Memory is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track one of the Xenoblade 2: Torna ~ The Golden Country Original Soundtrack, and track one of disc eleven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It is a piano arrangement of A Moment of Eternity. This song plays on the title screen for .

The False Queens is a track from , composed by Kenji Hiramatsu. It is track thirteen of disc five on the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track thirteen of disc sixteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the battles against the Queen of Keves and the Queen of Agnus.

The Great Sea Stirs is a track from , composed by ACE. It is track sixteen of disc seven from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track sixteen of disc eighteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays while riding the Bravery in Erythia Sea.

The Heroic Adventures is a track in , composed by Manami Kiyota. It is track seventeen of disc two from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track seventeen of disc seven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays when the party watches the play about the Aegis War in Fonsa Myma.

The Decision is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track twelve of disc four from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track twelve of disc nine from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It uses a motif from Elysium, in the Blue Sky. This song plays during the following moments: * When Jin kills Fan la Norne in Temperantia, and explains his hatred toward Indol. * When Pyra threatens to annihilate herself unless Jin spares Rex's life at the Genbu Crown. * When an enraged Akhos attacks Amalthus after Amalthus kills Patroka. * During the flashback of Klaus's experiment. In , this song plays when Jin arrives to protect Lora and Haze from being killed by Gort in Tori

The Towering Yggdrasil is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda and Kenji Hiramatsu. It is track six of disc two from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track six of disc seven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It uses a motif from Xenoblade II - Where It All Began -. This song plays during the following moments: * When the party steps out onto Outlook Knoll and looks at the view of Gormott. * When the party approaches the World Tree on Umon's Ship. * The arrival of the Indoline Titan Ship in Leftheria. * When Pandoria gets Genbu to surface from the Cloud Sea.

The Beginning of Darkness is a track from and , composed by ACE. It is track eighteen of disc two from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track eighteen of disc seven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments in : * Brighid's eavesdropping on Dughall's plans to capture Pyra. * When Dughall confronts the party on the Titan Battleship. * Pyra warning Rex to turn Umon's Ship around before being attacked by Ophion. * The party encountering a dead Titan in Uraya before being attacked by the Elder Arachno and Wulfric. * Akhos confronting the party in Garfont Village. * Zeke and Pandoria hiding from the party as they depart for Fonsa Myma

The Impending Crisis is a track from , composed by ACE. It is track four of disc four from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track four of disc nine from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * When Malos attacks Rex in the Chairman's Room. * When Lila fights Ardainian Soldiers on the rooftops of Alba Cavanich. * Jin's assault on the Urayan forces in Temperantia. * The party's discussion on how to stop Aeshma's attack. * Bana blows up Giga Rosa after his defeat in Indol. * Genbu begins to dive deeper into the Cloud Sea after the Omega Fetter is damaged. * Malos summons Ophion and reprograms it to listen to his orders. * Rex and Ni

The Past Revealed is a track from and , composed by ACE. It is track eleven of disc four from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track eleven of disc nine from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments in : * When Rex awakens after he and Pyra wash up in Gormott. * Jac's siblings plead with him to not try becoming a Driver. * Mòrag being notified by Aegaeon about Jin's attack on a shipment of Core Crystals. * When the party learns of the bandits' plans to attack Torigoth. * Amalthus and Mythra's conversation about his decision to aid Rex in his quest to reach Elysium. * Queen Raqura's reflection on the events following the Indoline summ

The Exhausted Victorious, The Speechless Defeated is a track from , composed by Yutaka Kunigo. It is track five of disc one from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track five of disc twelve from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the cutscene when Colony 9 is victorious over Colony Sigma. It also plays multiple times during Doing It My Way.

Those Who Devour Life is a track from , composed by Manami Kiyota. It is track ten of disc three from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track ten of disc fourteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * When Colony 9's forces look over the entrance to Alfeto Valley during Chapter 1. * When K arrives at Colony 4. * When the party notices the gold Flame Clock of Colony 18 at the Old Kana Battlefield. * When the party is in Colony Lambda until they help all of the unconscious soldiers. * When Shania overlooks the party as they consider the risks of infiltrating Keves Castle. * When a hooded Mio speaks with Noah when he's Amidst

The Two Off-Seers is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track six of disc two from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track six of disc thirteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * During Noah and Mio's battle in Alfeto Valley. * The party's first encounter with Juniper during Natural Selection. * The party's loss against N. * When Ashera takes on Zoren, Clad, and Easel during The Wrath of Ashera. * When the party realizes they fell for a trap during Side Story: Lanz. * As the area theme during Colony Gamma's training maneuvers on Everblight Plain during Shadow of Enmity In , this song plays during the foll
The Home of the Soul is a Blade Quest in . This quest involves MOMO, and is available after unlocking MOMO's level 4 Key Affinity and after defeating Giga Rosa.
Thermal Resistance is a stat in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It displays resistance to thermal-type attacks.
Thermal Attack Down is a debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It reduces thermal attack damage.

Tokilos King Eggs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by the Tokilos on Bionis' Leg and in Tephra Cave, and cannot be traded for. According to their description, they are eggs laid by the king of all birds and they are considered a food containing all nutrients. One is required to complete level 5 Nature in the reconstruction of Colony 6, and another for Replica Monado 5. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 6,800 Noponstones.

This quest will expire after the events of the Mechonis Core. To Colony 6! (Japanese: , Iza, Koronī 6 e, Now, to Colony 6) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Dulland at the main entrance to the ruined Colony 6, once Otharon has left for Alcamoth after the party met Miqol in the Hidden Machina Village. It is nearly identical to The Road Home, since they are Mutually Exclusive Quests, the biggest difference being the reward.

Tranquil Square (Japanese: , Kyojū-ku Ikoi no Hiroba) is a landmark in . It is located in the Residential District of Colony 9. It is an open space featuring some benches surrounding a tree and some house fronts. Betty and Françoise can be found here for most of the day (6:00 - 15:00) and Kenny Rohan is here from 9:00 - 15:00. There are also several nameless NPCs — a Nopon, a woman swooning over Kenny in the day, and a couple sitting on the benches at night.

Topple Plus (Japanese: , Tentō Jikan Purasu, Topple Time Plus) is a Gem in that increases the duration of Topple on enemies. The Battle Arts that are affected by this gem include: *Demon Slayer *Final Cross *Monado Cyclone *Roly-Poly *Starlight Kick *Steel Strike *Wild Down This Gem type should not be confused with "Topple Up", a gem that increases the damage dealt to a toppled enemy. __TOC__

Tinted Glasses (Japanese: , Karādo Gurasu) are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. These glasses can only be obtained through completing quests. Only two Tinted Glasses can be obtained per playthrough, as only one of the Miss Sweetness' Gratitude quests can be completed in each playthrough.

Tortas (Japanese: , Tōtā) are giant tortoise-like enemies in and . This species is close to the Tude. Tortas can be found outside Colony 9, on the Bionis' Leg, in Satorl Marsh, and on the Bionis' Shoulder.

The Tranquil Grotto (Japanese: , Shijima no Iwaya) is a location in . It is located on the lower level of Bionis' Leg. It is a cave semi-filled with water found at the southeast corner of the map. It can only be reached by swimming through Raguel Lake, but can be hard to access as there is an Envy Sardi directly within the cave entrance. Inside is an altar which the party must place flowers on for the Frontier Village quest Legendary Nopon Charm. The Medicinal Herb, which is required for the Bionis' Leg quest Spirits Raised, is also collected from around here. There is a water Ether Deposit here.

The Tirkin Headquarters (Japanese: , Tākin no Hon'ei) is a location in . It is located on the lower level of Bionis' Leg. As its name implies, it is the center of Tirkin operations, and the Vagrant Alfead, a Unique Monster, can be found here. It is located north of Rho Oasis, and must be accessed through a cave guarded by Tirkins. Clothes must be recovered from here during the quest Thieving Monsters. Every type of Tirkin on Bionis' Leg can be found here.

Traveller's Rest (Japanese: , Tabibito no Kyūsoku Atochi) is a location in . It is located on the upper level of Bionis' Leg. It is located directly west from Spiral Valley, and just above the Maguel Road entrance to the upper level. There is only a small campfire where two Nopon, Gerugu and Batubatu, can be found. They give the party some of the quests for Bionis' Leg, and unlike most of the quests these are not timed.

The Trader's Stopover (Japanese: , Taishō Chūkeiji) is a location in . It is located in Tephra Cave, just southeast of the Heavenly Window. The entrance of the room is guarded by the Erratic Goliante. This place houses a Key Item for the quest Securing Provisions, the Trader's Spare Key guarded by the Satisfied Gogol.

Titan Plates are heavy torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. There are only two available per playthrough. One can be obtained after completing the Colony 6 Reconstruction with level five in all categories. The other can be found in the Giant chest at Three Sage Summit.
The Titan Arms are heavy arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are obtained after leveling up Commerce to level five during the Colony 6 reconstruction.
The Titan Greaves are heavy legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in the Giant chest at Three Sage Summit during The Final Giants' Ruins.
Titan Guarders (Japanese: , Taitangādā) are weapons in They are gunlances wielded by Reyn, and can be obtained from varous high-level enemies. Titan Guarders are not otherwise available.

Transmission Bypass (Japanese: , Dōryoku Dentatsu Baipasu Nyūshu) is a quest in . It is one of the three quests that is co-triggered upon accepting quest Stunted Growth received from Orkatix at the northeast ledge of the Hidden Machina Village from the Junks.
Thunderclaps (Japanese: , Jinrai) are weapons in . They are rifles that can be wielded by Sharla.

The Tomb Robber Pool (Japanese: , Hakaarashi no Ike) is a landmark in . It is located on the first basement floor of the High Entia Tomb. This is the pool that the party falls into after Reyn touched the panel in the Sealed Chamber that was meant to be verified by a High Entia (or someone carrying the blood of a High Entia).
The Tower of Trials - Bridge (Japanese: , Shiren no Tō: Renrakukyō) is a landmark in . It is located on the second basement floor of the High Entia Tomb.

The Tomb Approach (Japanese: , Bosho no Sandō) is a landmark in . It is the first landmark in the High Entia Tomb, located on the ground floor. It is a fairly short and narrow tunnel that leads to the Sealed Chamber.

The Transformer Area (Japanese: , Koyubi Hen'atsu-ku) is a location in . It is on the lower level of the Fallen Arm south of the Wreckage Beach, and can be accessed from there. Shulk and Fiora visit shortly after arriving at the Fallen Arm to look for the others. A path from here leads south west to the Ulna Passage, where they meet up with Reyn and Sharla.

Topple Up (Japanese: , Tentō Iryoku Appu) is a Gem in that increases damage dealt to Toppled enemies. This Gem type should not be confused with "Topple Plus", a gem that lengthens the duration of the Topple status effect. __TOC__

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Together Forever (Japanese: , Itsumademo Kimi to Isshoni) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Scarlen at the Main Entrance of Alcamoth. Scarlen asks the party to deliver his letter by talking to Rozeal. This quest is triggered by talking to Rozeal first (B route) then to Ricoth in How Do I Feel?. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment. This quest and I Love You No Matter What are mutually exclusive. The route choice made during How Do I Feel? determines which quest will be available.

Tirkins (Japanese: , Tākin, alternate plural form Tirkin) are a recurring species of primitve but sentient bird-like humanoids in the . They are a type of enemy in , , and , and are both a race and an enemy family in and . Tirkins are similar in appearance to, and may be related to, Chilkins, which look like white Tirkins, and Gulkins, which look like blue Tirkins with a different beak and an amphibious lifestile. In , white Tirkins appear in cold regions, but they are not referred as Chilkins. Aside from equipment and color, all Tirkins have the same appearance. Totems can buff some Tirkin enemies in a similar manner to Standards.

Tokilos Wings are rare materials in . They are only dropped by Dark Murakmor in Colony 9, or can be traded for with Kantz and Dionysis. According to their description, they are magnificently mesmerising feathers that only sprout in the breeding season.
Tough Bunnit Woods are rare materials in . They are dropped by Bunnits on Tephra Hill in Colony 9, and can also be traded for.

Tirkin Crests are rare materials in . They can be dropped by various Tirkins on Bionis' Leg, or traded for in the Refugee Camp and Colony 6. According to their description, they are beautiful well-kept crests that are highly functional and even have pockets. Two are needed for Material Quest 2 (Bionis' Leg).
Topple Resist (Japanese: , Tentō Teikō) is a Gem in that increases resistance to Topple. __TOC__

This quest will expire after the events at the Meyneth Shrine. To My Loved One... (Japanese: , Aisuru Hito e) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Zarkort south of Digit 2 on the Fallen Arm after completing For My Loved One.... If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment. It will expire after the events at the Meyneth Shrine.

The Training Ground Roof (Japanese: , Enshūjō Okujō) is a location in . It is a partially hidden area in the Central Factory on Mechonis. It can be reached by jumping off the north end of the Central Lift while it is in motion and onto a ledge a short distance below. Roof Battle becomes available immediately upon discovering the location.

Trainer Harmelon (Japanese: , Chōkyō no Hāmerun) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Tirkin family that appears on Bionis' Leg, on the high hill east of Zax Guidepost, accompanied by two Berserk Ardun. It must be defeated as part of the Challenge 2 - Part 1 quest. It can drop Tirkin Crests, which are required for Material Quest 2 in the Refugee Camp.

Tranquil Morax (Japanese: , Heion no Morakusu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon and can be found at level 50 in Sword Valley. It is located inside the Enalda Control Base. The party must defeat it to complete the Secure Enalda Control Base surprise quest.

Trainer Tirkins (Japanese: , Torēnā Tākin) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Tirkin family, and can be found from level 15 to 17 southeast of Spiral Valley on Bionis' Leg. They can drop the Tirkin Crests needed for Material Quest 2.

Timed Quests are quests in that expire after certain events, such as the migration to Colony 6 and the Mechonis Core event. These quests must be completed before the event. There are 130 Timed Quests, 18 are listed Mutually Exclusive Quests, 9 are Surprise Quests. These quests are designated as timed by which indicates that the quest may expire. Completing certain story events or completing a different exclusive quest can cause a quest to expire. Note: All of Sword Valley's (4), Mechonis Field's (4), Central Factory's (4) and Agniratha's (14) quests are timed. All Alcamoth's quests (55) are also timed, with the exception of Vidian Rescue Mission. There are no timed quests in . :※ Only timed

Tramont Wisps (Japanese: , Toramonto Ranpusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Wisp family, and can be found at levels 53-55 on Digit 2 Plain on the Fallen Arm. They only appear on clear nights. They can drop the Wisp Bliss Rings needed for En Argentis' Betrothal Test.

The Top-Secret Orders are a Key Item in . They are needed to complete Sylviane's branch of Financial Planning (B route). They can be found in the water below the Central Plaza in Colony 9, but only if Sylviane's branch of the quest is active.

Tirkin Tail Feathers are rare materials in . They are dropped by Tirkins on Bionis' Leg and can be traded for in the Refugee Camp and in Colony 6. According to their description, they are feathers that feel nice on the skin and they would make great quill pens. Two of them are needed for Material Quest 2 on Bionis' Leg.
The Torn Paper is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is the object of Search Quest 2 on Bionis' Leg. It can be found on a cliff far south of Jabos Rock Rest Area.

The Trader's Spare Key is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found in the Trader's Stopover in Tephra Cave. It is required for Securing Provisions and guarded by the quest exclusive Satisfied Gogol.

The Top-Secret Data is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received from Daza as a reward for completing Secret Mission, and is needed during Find the Kingpin. It is received again from Gadada during Adviser Hunt.

The Timer is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. Along with the Electrical Fuse and the Ether Explosive, it is one of three items required to complete Materials for a Bomb. It can be obtained by defeating the Offensive Scout on a catwalk west of the Central Lift in the Central Factory.

Tirkin Elder Medals are rare materials in . They can only be dropped by the Field Altrich on the Bionis' Leg, and is not available for trade. According to their description, they are considered the most esteemed Tirkin award and they allow the holder to engage in polygamy. One is needed for Replica Monado 4.

The Tower Boarding Gate (Japanese: , Chūō-tō Tōjōguchi) is a landmark in . It is located on the third floor of the Central Factory, east of the Central Tower Roof. The Sinful Lamorak can be found here. To the northwest is an Ether Crystal Deposit containing Attack Plus IV and Debuff Plus IV crystals.

To the Central Tower (Japanese: , Chūōtō wo Mezase) is a Story Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received automatically when the party reaches the Central Gate while arriving at the Central Factory and having left the elevator at Port Terminal.

The Top Housing Level (Japanese: , Kōsō Jūtaku-ban) is a location in . It is located on the sixth floor of Frontier Village, and is the highest level of housing in the village. The Chief's Residence is on this level. The Shiny Ball, needed for Search Quest 3, can be found here.

Tornado Elements are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Wind Nebulae in Satorl Marsh, or traded for with Kacha. According to their description, they are wind elements that can be buried in the ground to cause a tornado.

Time Mushrooms are objects in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are large mushrooms which the Nopon of Frontier Village use as clocks. There are three Time Mushrooms, located on floors 1F, 4F, and 7F. Migaga is in charge of their caretaking, and asks the party to fertilise them when they malfunction during Fixing Time Mushrooms.
Tough Parts M are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from various Mechon in Mechonis Field. Tough Parts M are not available for trade.
Tough Parts L are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from M84/GRUNT, M91/DOGMA, and M76/MOIST units in Mechonis Field. Tough Parts L are not available for trade.
Thunder Elements are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Nebulae in Colony 6, or be traded for with Jer'ell or Neonik.
Tough Parts S are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from various Mechon in Mechonis Field. They are not available for trade.

The Time Bomb is a Key Item in . It is made out of an Electrical Fuse, Ether Explosive and a Timer from the Weapon Creation Panel of Central Factory for Find a Path to the Top, and is used to create an entrance through the Factory Vent.

The Tokilos' Egg is a key item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is required for With Much Gratitude and will only appear after the quest has been accepted. It can be found on Bionis Leg, on a lower ledge near Zax Guidepost. This ledge can be reached by climbing down two sets of vines to the east of Zax Guidepost.
Tornado Blade is a Longsword Battle Art in . It attacks enemies in a circle around the caster, launching small enemies as a side effect.

]] Treasure Boxes are objects in . They are dropped by monsters after they are defeated, or they can be discovered in a few places of Mira's areas, using the Aerial Cam, the Research Probe or the related Segment Map's Topic tool. They are equivalent to the Treasure Chests in . There are three types of treasure obtainable from enemies, bronze, silver or gold drops. The Treasure Sensor augment can increase the quality of enemy treasure. Treasure boxes come in a variety of forms, and require a certain Field-Skill to open. Earth-based containers, vehicles, and White Whale debris are opened with Mechanical skill. Native structures like insect nests, strange trees, and indigen dung require the Bio

Treasure Deal was a game mechanic in which allowed Armor, Weapons, or Augments received as battle rewards to be offered to other members of the Squad. When the Treasure Boxes dropped by an enemy after a battle were opened, the player may offer one of the contents as a Treasure Deal. If there were multiple valid Treasure Deal options, a player could choose to offer one Treasure Deal and then wait a few minutes to then enter and exit the Choose Items menu. After exiting the Choose Items, menu, if enough time has elapsed, a player may treasure deal another valid item. After the online shutdown, the Treasure Deal mechanic was discontinued. Though online gameplay has become possible again with th

Towering Shadow (巨大な影, Gigantic Silhouette) is an Event Track in , composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 2 of disc 2 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is a dark, ominous theme that is heard in the following cutscenes: * The party reaches the base level of the Central Pit. (The music is later interrupted by Engage the Enemy.) * When Alvis meets Zanza after Emperor Sorean's death. Theme is later interrupted by Egil's theme. * The party tells Dickson about Fiora's survival and Mumkhar's betrayal when he meets them with a Supply Convoy in Sword Valley, after which he and Alvis depart. * The party confronts Mumkhar at the Heavy Machine Depot in Sword Valley. * Egil
Titan Recharge is one of Frye's two Signature Arts in . It is obtained as a reward for completing the Affinity Mission Brotherly Love.
Tranquilliser (Japanese: , Surīpu Baretto, Sleep Bullet) is one of Sharla's Ether arts in . It may put an enemy to Sleep. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called Tranquilsnooze.

Tourteau, the Delectable (Japanese: , Gokuuma no Turutō) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 8 at Cliffside Beach in Primordia at night. Defeating it is required for the eponymous Basic Mission Tourteau, the Delectable.
Translucent Ciniculas (Japanese: , Kuria Vasaruto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Cinicula family, and can be found at level 25-26 at East Ciel Sandsea in Sylvalum.

Tough Armored Suids (Japanese: , Hādo Āmā Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 41-50 northwest of FN Site 103 in Primordia. They have been domesticated and armored by the Prone. Two of them must be defeated during Elma's Task C.

Trained Armored Suids (Japanese: , Torein Āmā Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 24 or 27-30 outside Rooney Cavern in Oblivia. They have been domesticated and armored by the Prone.
The Titan's Table (Japanese: , Kyojin no Tēburu) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Cauldros, east of the Scholes Battlegrounds and south of the Emerian Battlegrounds.
Toppler is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when a character topples an enemy by using a Battle Art such as Assault Hammer.

Toxic Mortifoles (Japanese: , Tokishikku Foriumu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Mortifole family, and can be found at level 41-45 at the eastern sides of Aaroy Plain and South Coast in Oblivia.
Thunder Duoguills (Japanese: , Sandā Guira) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Duoguill family and can be found at level 25-29 in Oblivia, west of FN Site 313.

Transport Pilots are NPCs in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are female or male pilots found in different locations, including the Central Industrial District, the BLADE Tower in the Administrative District, the North Founders Street in the Commercial District, and Deliverance Park in the Residential District. They are responsible for piloting the airship, the primary method of reaching the upper level of the Administrative District from other parts of New Los Angeles. They do not appear on the Affinity Chart.
The Titan's Table BC (Japanese: , Kyojin no Tēburu BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a BLADE basecamp located in Cauldros, run by the Interceptors.
Tika (English dub: ) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found in the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles.
Tracey is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found near Barista Court in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles. She is a member of the Mediators Division.

Ton'barac is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Sports Complex in the Residential District of New Los Angeles. He found and trade a Gold Nopopotamus Card required to complete Trade Agreement.
To Serve Nopon (Japanese: , Iseijin no Reshipi Atsume!, Collection of Alien Recipes!) is an Affinity Mission in . It can be accepted in the BLADE Barracks in New Los Angeles.

Titanium Oc-servs (Japanese: , Chitan Me-Tsuu) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Oc-serv machines, and can be found at level 51-53 or at level 58 in Sylvalum's Quay Hollows or Banshee Cave.
Tractor Beetles (Japanese: , Torakutabītoru) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia. Twenty-four are required for A Novel Proposal.
Timid Sunflowers (Japanese: , Mōn Himawari) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.

Tough Blattas (Japanese: , Hādo Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 21-28 in Primordia, southeast of FN Site 110. Ten must be defeated to complete Arms and the Man.

Tornado Jaculs (Japanese: , Torunēdo Hasutara) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Jacul family, and can be found at level 51-57 around the north and northeast side of Mount M'gando in Cauldros.
Tobias (Japanese: , Tobiasu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is located at the Central Industrial District in New Los Angeles, near the Repenta Diner.

Toy Monoceros (Japanese: , Hobī Unikoru, Hobby Monoceros) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Monoceros family, and can be found at level 8 in Cauldros, northwest of FN Site 505 on the path leading down to the sea.
Tormenta, the Scarlet-Clad (Japanese: , Hiodoshi no Torumenta) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Turba family. It can be found at level 41 in Noctilum at Decapotamon.

Tico, the Precious (Japanese: , Torame no Tiko) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Blatta family. It can be found at level 26-30 inside the cavity of Beehive Rock in Oblivia.
Topaz Arenatects (Japanese: , Topāzu Rorongu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Arenatect family, and can be found at level 55 at Banshee Cave in Sylvalum.

Tidal Purgovents (Japanese: , Taidaru Morumu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Purgovent family, and can be found at level 38-40 in the Vitriol Cesspool and Weeping Whitewood in Noctilum.
Thunder Scintimures (Japanese: , Sandā Torizumo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Scintimure family, and can be found at level 41-50 in Cauldros's Titan's Table.

Treasure Sensors are armor Augments in and which increase the rate at which enemies drop gold Treasure Boxes, which have higher rates of rarer and better items. Different enemies have different base rates for gold drop, so to guarantee it, different amounts of bonus Treasure Sensor are needed. As a general guide, Tyrants need 50, and normal enemies need 95, however, not all enemies follow this pattern.

Topple: Decoy is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It gives a chance to activate Decoy after an enemy attempts to topple a character with this augment. Training Troubles is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the back of the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles between Lao and Cross at night.
The Toxic Chemical Bomb is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is received from Pfeffen during A Dubious Operation.

These missions allow players to fight against certain Bosses and attempt to beat their best time. They all have a time limit of 15 minutes and a maximum of 4 party members. They also have a limit of 3 retries, allowing an incapacitated player to be revived and continue the mission. The Title Screen is an area in . It is used only during the game's title screen, and is not used in cutscenes nor visited in normal gameplay. It is a seemingly endless plain, with the Monado sticking out of the ground and the remains of a Mechon to one side. Like the cutscenes in this game, the title screen is rendered in-engine rather than pre-rendered, so this location is stored in the game’s data as a 3D space. Its internal filename is ma0000, and it has the same format as other areas like Colony 9. The Monado and Mechon debris are not part of the map model, but are added as separate props during rendering. Topple is a status in and . It causes a targeted enemy to fall down and removes its resistance to Daze. When a target is down, it cannot dodge and thus all attacks against it have 100% accuracy. Furthermore, against a toppled target, critical damage is increased by 25% and all ether attacks will always land critical hits. When hit with a topple art, an enemy will remain toppled for three seconds; if hit with another topple art within that time, the time will be extended. Arts that inflict topple are colored green. Some enemies have a topple spike, which damages or debuffs party members that attack the enemy while it is toppled.
Tough Tendons are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Sanjibal Behemoths.

Tora (Japanese: ) is one of the main playable characters in . He is a Nopon and the creator of the artificial Blade Poppi. Despite being the only party member incapable of being a Driver, he is the only one who can use the various forms of Poppi in battle. Tora joins the party after completing the main quests Artificial Blade Parts 1 and Artificial Blade Parts 2 during Chapter 2. Upon joining the party he is equipped with a common Nopon Mask. Tora was designed by Masatsugu Saito, the lead character designer of the game.

After the Ardainian occupation, the Torigoth Relay Base and Titan Battleship were set up to enforce the Empire's rule. At the time of the Aegis War, during the events of , Torigoth Village was a relatively minor location and not Gormott's capital, which was the White Chair.
Tiger! Tiger! is a minigame and mechanic in developed by Monolith Soft.

They can also be obtained from Salvage Points, upon a successful Salvaging of items sunk beneath the Cloud Sea. Treasure Troves can contain Gold, Accessories, Pouch Items, rare materials, etc. Some require Field Skills to be opened or revealed, usually "Lockpicking", "Fortitude", or "Earth Mastery". Treasure Troves come in five forms: small brown chests, small red chests, small red barrels, small silver chests, and large white chests. Tranquility (Japanese: , Annon) is a Blade Quest in . It can be received from Vess at Torigoth Market in the Gormott Province during the day.
Titan-Oil Hand Creams are Cosmetic Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Aquaneze Cosmetics in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Brighid.

Tora's House (Japanese: , Tora no Ie) is a Landmark in . It is located on the lower level of Torigoth in the Gormott Province, on the second-to-bottom level of the Galad Residential Zone. It is the home of Tora, where he has been working on his Artificial Blade, Poppi. His house has both a kitchen for Pyra and Crossette to use their Cooking skills, as well as the console to play Tiger! Tiger!. A forestry Collection Point is found near the latter. Starting in Chapter 5, Tatazo and Lila can be found here.
The Torigoth Base Entrance (Japanese: , Torigo Kichi Seimon) is a Landmark in . It is the primary entrance to the Torigoth Relay Base in the Gormott Province.
The Torigoth Market (Japanese: , Torigo Shōtengai) is a Location in . It is located in Torigoth in the Gormott Province, past the Torigoth Arch.

The Torigoth Relay Base (Japanese: , Superubia-gun Torigo Kichi) is a location in . It is located east of Torigoth in the Gormott Province, between the Connecting Bridge and the Torigoth Base Entrance. It is the primary military facility of the Empire of Mor Ardain in the Gormott Province.

The Trailblazers' Bridge (Japanese: , Senkusha-tachi no Hashi) is a Location in . It is located on the Lower Level of the Gormott Province and connects Wrecc Marshland to Masrah Spring via the Old Ghostwood Road. A fallen tree here must be cleared using Pyra's Fire Mastery. There are no enemies on the bridge itself; those listed here are in the unnamed area between Wrecc Marshland and the bridge.

The Traveler's Resting Tree (Japanese: , Tabibito no Tomarigi) is a landmark in . It is a massive tree located in the middle of the Nocclia Woods on the right side of the upper level of the Gormott Province. There are no enemies here.

The Torigoth Flower Patch (Japanese: , Torigo no Hanabatake) is a landmark in . It is located at the far front of the right area on the upper level of Gormott Province. The flower patch marks the exact spot of what was once Torigoth Cemetery, the final resting place of the residents of Torigoth Village who were massacred by Coeian soldiers during the Aegis War. There is a Salvage Point here.

The Training Ground (Japanese: , Isamashi no Shūrenjō) is a location in . It is located in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya, under the terrace that leads to the rear gate. There are no enemies here except during story and quest events.

The Titan Weapon Remains (Japanese: , Kyoshinjū Heiki no Nakigara) are a location in . They are a dead Judicium Titan found on the Central Plain of Temperantia as the remnants of the battle against Aeshma's Core, directly below Haggle's Swordtip. The Leaning Tower of Dorrick is nearby to the east.

The Titan Weapon Dig Site (Japanese: , Kyoshinjū Heiki Hakkutsugenba) is a landmark in . It is located at the Ruins of Judicium in Temperantia, before the Lost Capital Judicium. The Heart-to-Heart "Reconciliation" can be viewed atop the first Judicium Titan.

The Titan Battleship (Japanese: , Kyoshinjū Senkan) is a recurring level in . It is an Ardainian Titan ship located in the Gormott Province, moored at the Torigoth Relay Base. For a brief period at the beginning of Chapter 6, it can also be found in the Indoline Praetorium, moored at Goetuis Wharf #2, where it is also called "Ardainian Battleship", "Ardainian Titan Battleship" or "Titan Warship". Although the Battleship is initially full of hostile Ardainian Soldiers, these later disappear, leaving the only enemies in the Battleship the two Unique Monsters, who are both prisoners.

Time is Money is a quest in . It can be received at Corinne's House in the Leftherian Archipelago, after sending a total of 90,000G to Corinne and speaking to Max again, after completing Chapter 6. It should be noted that the 90,000G sent during Big Job Preparations does not count.

Traveling Bards are NPCs and shops in and . They appear in New Game Plus, which requires the Version 1.3.0 update or later. They appear at various locations throughout Alrest, and are displayed on the map as green shop icons. They can be male or female characters of any race. Traveling Bards exchange Bonus EXP for valuable items; for example Accessory Expander Kits can be obtained from the bard in Goldmouth. The Version 1.4.0 update added several more Traveling Bards who trade various Role CPUs for Poppi.

Tome of Morytha Vol. 2 (Japanese: , Morusu no Komonjo Nikan no Kaidoku) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild automatically after obtaining the Tome of Morytha #2. The tome can be purchased from the Reedirait Bookstore. The time required to complete this mission is 20 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 5 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Electric Mastery", "Forestry" and "Ancient Wisdom" Field Skills.

Tome of Morytha Vol. 4 (Japanese: , Morusu no Komonjo Yonkan no Kaidoku) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild automatically after obtaining the Tome of Morytha #4. The tome can be obtained in an auction held by Pilopilo to the northwest of the Central Exchange while Adenine is in the party. The time required to complete this mission is 20 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 5 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Earth Mastery", "Ichthyology" and "Ancient Wisdom" Field Skills.

Tinglip Drinks are Drink Pouch items in . They can be prepared from a recipe requiring five Cranberry Bells and five Panda Pansies at Rumbletum Canteen in the Argentum Trade Guild during the quest Fame and Family.

Tilde is an NPC in . She is an Urayan who can be found in the Gwenith Paddies at Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. She offers the Merc Mission Dream of Rice. She usually always talks about tending to the rice crops and expresses continued patriotic support and agreement with the Urayan military and government's restrictions and rationing of produce.

Thunderslam (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using a Brilliant Twinblades. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Zeke's Righteous Guillotine.
Torcall is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian soldier who can be found at the Ardainian Garrison in Temperantia. Torcall offers no quests or Merc Missions.

Tirkin Crabs are Key Items in . They can be made at the DLC Shop Famed Gourmet Chefs run by the Head Fire Dragon and a Fire Dragons Member at the Bellyfull Canteen in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the DLC Quest Midnight Feasting upon installing the New Quests Pack 1 of the Expansion Pass.

Tirkin Curries are Key Items in . They can be purchased from the DLC Shops Famed Gourmet Chefs run by the Head Fire Dragon and a Fire Dragons Member at the Bellyfull Canteen in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the DLC Quest Midnight Feasting upon installing the New Quests Pack 1 of the Expansion Pass.

Toutour is an NPC in . He is a Nopon entrepreneur who can be found by Port Anangham in the Empire of Mor Ardain. As a tour guide, Toutour speaks in full sentences with proper grammar rather than the Noponic dialect used by most Nopon. He gives the DLC quest Industrial Sort of Tour.
The Top Secret Papers are an Info Item in . It can be obtained as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Stolen Data, or purchased from the Mor Ardain Informant for 2,000 G.

Tolulu is an NPC in . She is a Nopon who can be found at Blossomshade Cliff in the Kingdom of Uraya during the Blade Quest All's Fair. She can only be found early in the morning between 5:00 and 7:00 at Blossomshade Cliff, but can be found anytime at Mymoma Playhouse upon completion of the quest.

Tora's Angst is a Heart-to-Heart in . It can be found at the top of the tree in at the Farlaine Central Pools in the Kingdom of Uraya. Level 2 "Wind Mastery" and "Leaping" Field Skills are required in order to reach it. If the party rests at Harghalgh Inn before viewing this Heart-to-Heart, Tora will direct the party to its location.
Titan Illuminations are Art Pouch items in . They can be made by Dahlia using her "Icecraft Lv.3" field skill at the Dahlia's Icecraft table in Argentum's Goldmouth Warehouse.
